newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk court to investigate charges against Ciller.
newsitem.headline: Turk court to investigate charges against Ciller.

text.p: A court is to investigate charges that former foreign minister Tansu Ciller accepted money from abroad to work against Turkey's national interests during her four years in government, a court spokesman said on Tuesday.

Turkey's chief prosecutor Vural Savas has asked Ankara Security Court to look into allegations by the leader of a far-left party that Ciller worked for foreign intelligence agencies from 1974, prosecutor Arif Gurses told Reuters.

Workers Party chairman Dogu Perincek accused Ciller in a petition to the prosecutor of "accepting money and benefits from foreigners with the intention of acting against the national interest", the state-run agency said.
He also said U.S.-educated economist Ciller had "disclosed information which should be kept secret for the state's security," the agency said.
Ciller played down the charges when asked about them on Tuesday.
"All of these are small things, the important thing is the continuation of our cause," Ciller said in response to a question.
She stepped down on Monday after a year as deputy prime minister and foreign minister in a coalition with Islamists.

She became Turkey's first woman prime minister in 1993 but Turkey's secularist establishment turned against her after she went into government with the Islamists, who later dropped damaging corruption charges against her in parliament.
The coalition collapsed last month under pressure from Turkey's powerful military amid accusations it was encouraging Islamic activism.
Ciller's longstanding political rival Mesut Yilmaz was named prime minister on Monday in a new left-right alliance.
